# Start work in the right directory

## Problem statement

When `wl ampa start-work` provisions and enters a *fresh* dev container, the
interactive shell is started with an explicit `cd` to the container-local
sandbox path (`/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`) instead of the canonical
`/workdir/project` symlink. Any already-claimed container is re-entered with
`cd /workdir/project`, so the initial entry is inconsistent with re-entry,
confuses the shell prompt (it computes its relative path against
`/workdir/project`), and makes tooling or user commands that assume
`/workdir/project` report the wrong location.

## Users

- **AI agents** launched into a container by `wl ampa start-work`: they expect
  the project to be at `/workdir/project` so scripts, prompts and `wl ampa
  finish-work` resolve consistently.
- **Operators** reviewing/spawning sandboxes: they expect the documented
  `/workdir/project` path to hold regardless of whether the container was just
  created or re-entered.

### Example user stories

- As an AI agent, when I am dropped into a fresh dev container, I want to be in
  `/workdir/project` so that relative paths, the prompt and tooling match every
  other entry point.
- As an operator, when I run `wl ampa start-work <id>` and then `pwd`, I want to
  see `/workdir/project`, not a `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl ampa start-work <work-item-id>` (and its `sw` alias) starts the
  interactive shell in `/workdir/project` for a newly-provisioned container,
  i.e. `pwd` inside the container reports `/workdir/project` (verification:
  manual E2E `wl ampa sw <id>` then `pwd`).
- [ ] Initial entry is consistent with the already-implemented re-entry and
  legacy-container paths, which both `cd /workdir/project` (verification: code
  inspection + assertion that all interactive entry commands reference
  `/workdir/project`).
- [ ] The shell prompt's relative-path segment resolves against
  `/workdir/project` (no leading `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` shown) and
  `/etc/ampa_bashrc` continues to `cd /workdir/project` (verification: manual
  E2E prompt check).
- [ ] An automated regression test asserts that the interactive entry command
  changes into `/workdir/project` and not the container-local
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` path; the test fails against the
  pre-fix code and passes after the fix (verification: `npm test` /
  `node --test` in the ampa project).
- [ ] Behaviour of `wl ampa finish-work` and the `--wait` / re-entry flows is
  unchanged (verification: existing ampa test suite green).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The container project is physically cloned to
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`; `/workdir/project` is a symlink to it
  created by the setup script. The fix must not move the physical clone.
- Must keep the existing pool/template provisioning, `wl sync` and prompt
  behaviour intact.
- Change is confined to the ampa plugin's `startWork` entry command; the ampa
  project is the implementation repository (see open questions).

## Existing state

- The `start-work` implementation moved out of this repository: the
  `skill/install-ampa/` skill and `ampa.mjs` plugin now live in the **ampa**
  repository (`git@github.com:SorraTheOrc/ampa.git`), under
  `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs`. It was removed from SorraAgents in
  commit `ae0d8474` ("install_ampa skill is now in the ampa proejct itself",
  2026-04-10); the `ampa-repo` git submodule pointer was also removed.
- The container setup clones to `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` and
  creates the symlink `/workdir/project` → that path; `/etc/ampa_bashrc` already
  ends with `cd /workdir/project`.
- Re-entry paths (`start-work` on a claimed pool container / legacy
  `ampa-<id>`) use `cd /workdir/project 2>/dev/null; … exec bash --login`.
- The initial interactive entry in `startWork` used
  `cd ${containerProjectRoot} && exec bash --login` (the `/tmp` path).
- **A fix already exists in the ampa repository on `origin/dev`**: commit
  `77856e0` ("fix: use canonical /workdir/project in start-work initial entry
  (SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW)") changes that one line to
  `cd /workdir/project && exec bash --login`. The matching branch is
  `wl-SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW-fix-start-work-directory`. It is **not yet on
  `main`** (normal dev→main release flow) and the local ampa `dev` checkout is
  one commit behind `origin/dev`.
- The fix commit contains **no automated test** and has not updated the manual
  E2E expectations.

## Desired change

Enter a freshly-provisioned dev container in the canonical
`/workdir/project` directory, matching the re-entry paths, and add regression
coverage so the initial-entry path cannot silently diverge again.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs` (ampa repository) — `startWork()`
  initial interactive entry (`distrobox enter … -c 'cd /workdir/project &&
  exec bash --login'`, currently line ~2137 on the fix branch). Also
  `buildContainerSetupScript()` / `/etc/ampa_bashrc` writer if the canonical
  path is factored out.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-devcontainer.mjs` (ampa repository) — add/extend a
  regression test for the entry command.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-start-work-template-escape.mjs` (ampa repository) —
  nearby start-work setup-script assertions if the path is interpolated.
- `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` (ampa repository) — manual E2E
  expectations / documentation of `/workdir/project`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the fix belongs in the ampa repository, since that is where
  `start-work` lives today; the SorraAgents reference in the commit message is
  the originating work-item ID.
- **Risk:** adding an automated test may require refactoring the entry command
  out of `startWork` into a small exported helper (the command is currently
  built inline and spawned directly), otherwise it is only testable via the
  manual E2E script. Mitigation: extract a pure helper (e.g.
  `buildEntryCommand(cName)`) and unit-test it.
- **Risk:** local ampa `dev` is behind `origin/dev`; implementing from the local
  checkout without pulling would recreate/conflict with the existing fix.
  Mitigation: start from the fix branch / `origin/dev`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** while in the entry code it is tempting to refactor the
  pool/template or prompt logic. Any such extra opportunity should be recorded
  as a separate linked work item, not folded into this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MLQ8Z6V20C2FPFP** — "start-work Subcommand" (completed) — defines the
  `wl ampa start-work` behaviour this work item corrects.
- **SA-0MLQ6ZLIO1THWA9O** — "Podman development container for SorraAgents"
  (completed) — parent epic; origin of the `/workdir/project` convention.
- **SA-0MLRGE8T01IHS922** — "When run wl ampa sw do a wl sync" (completed) —
  the `wl sync` behaviour on entry/re-entry, adjacent to this flow.
- **SA-0MLQ8ZT1300Q1MOM** — "list-containers Subcommand" (completed) — related
  container lifecycle command.
- ampa repository commit `77856e0` on `origin/dev` — the existing fix.

## Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The `start-work` code now lives in the ampa repository
  (`SorraTheOrc/ampa`), and the fix for this work item is already committed
  there on `origin/dev` (`77856e0`, referencing SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW), not yet on
  `main`. Should this SorraAgents work item (a) be closed as complete,
  documenting the ampa fix, (b) be migrated/copied to the ampa project's
  worklog (prefix `AM`), or (c) keep additional work in SorraAgents?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the SA implement skill runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree, where the ampa plugin no longer exists, so an
  implementer cannot make the change here without editing another repository.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The ampa fix is a one-line change with no automated
  regression test. Should this work item also add a test asserting the initial
  entry `cd`s to `/workdir/project` (which likely requires extracting the entry
  command into a testable helper), or is manual E2E coverage sufficient?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: no existing test asserts the
  entry command; `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` documents the path but
  is not automated.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** If the fix is accepted as already complete, should the
  SorraAgents work item still record the ampa commit hash/PR and be closed once
  the fix reaches ampa `main`, or closed immediately against `origin/dev`?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the global workflow normally
  closes work items only after the `dev`→`main` release.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MN1M2B810I9YC0U** – Validate Playwright Distrobox compatibility spike (completed)
- **SA-0MPON9P8Z0062VBL** – Child work items created by /plan should start at intake_complete stage (completed)
- **SA-0MKXYO42T0FC6IJR** – Isolated work environments for parallel work (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: container, directory, make, project, right (+3 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)

# Voice-to-text pi extension using faster-whisper (Ctrl+Space)

## Problem statement

Pi has no voice input, so operators must type long prompts by hand. We need a pi
extension that captures microphone audio, transcribes it locally with
[faster-whisper](https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper), streams the text
into the pi editor, and submits it automatically — toggled with a single
shortcut key.

## Users

Primary user: pi operators running the TUI on Linux/WSL2 with a CUDA GPU (the
requesting operator has an RTX 3050, 4 GB VRAM). Secondary user: any pi operator
who wants hands-free prompt entry.

Example user stories:

- As a pi operator, I press **Ctrl+Space**, speak my prompt, and it appears in
  the editor live, so I can dictate instead of typing.
- As a pi operator, when I stop speaking for a moment or press **Ctrl+Space**
  again, the prompt is sent exactly as if I had typed it and pressed Enter, so I
  don't have to touch the keyboard to submit.
- As a privacy-conscious operator, transcription runs entirely on my own
  machine (local GPU), so my audio never leaves my system.
- As an operator without CUDA, I can fall back to CPU inference by changing one
  setting.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In the pi TUI, pressing **Ctrl+Space** (configurable keybinding) starts
   microphone capture; the footer/status area shows a clear recording indicator.
2. While recording, partial transcription results are streamed into the pi
   editor and each new partial replaces the previous one; on completion the
   editor contains the final transcript.
3. Recording stops and the transcript is **submitted automatically** when
   either (a) Ctrl+Space is pressed again, or (b) the user has been silent for
   more than 3 seconds (configurable). Submission behaves the same as if the
   operator had typed the text and pressed Enter (a normal user message,
   respecting pi's busy/steering mode).
4. Transcription is performed locally by faster-whisper on the CUDA GPU
   (`float16`) through a persistent Python worker that loads the model once per
   session; model size, device and compute type are configurable
   (default: `small` + `cuda` + `float16`, with automatic CPU `int8` fallback
   when CUDA is unavailable).
5. Audio is captured as 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM through a configurable capture
   command (default works under WSLg/PulseAudio); if a required dependency is
   missing the extension shows an actionable notification and never crashes the
   pi session.
6. Unit tests cover the recording state machine, silence/pause detection,
   partial-transcript replacement, the Ctrl+Space toggle, and the worker
   protocol — without requiring a real microphone or GPU (capture and
   transcription are mocked).
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **TypeScript extension**, consistent with `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals`
  (jiti-loaded, no build step). Must use only the public `ExtensionAPI`.
- **Python bridge**: faster-whisper is Python-only, so the extension spawns a
  long-lived Python worker and talks to it over a line-delimited JSON protocol
  (model loaded once, not per utterance).
- **Platform**: Linux/WSL2 with CUDA. GPU target is an RTX 3050 with 4 GB VRAM —
  the default model must fit comfortably (`small`); `large-v3` may OOM and is
  not the default.
- **Local-only**: no cloud/network STT; privacy is a hard requirement.
- **Keybinding conflict risk**: Ctrl+Space is commonly intercepted by terminals
  and Windows IMEs, so the keybinding must be configurable and documented, with
  a recommended alternative.
- **WSL audio caveat**: WSL2 audio input requires WSLg/PulseAudio (or an
  ALSA→Pulse bridge). Capture backend must be selectable/overridable rather
  than hard-coded.

## Existing state

- Pi extension infrastructure already exists in this repo: `pi-client/` holds
  pi client extensions (`proxy-sse-signals`, `proxy-compaction-bridge`), each
  symlinked into `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` and unit-tested under `tests/unit/`
  with `node:test` (see `tests/unit/test-proxy-sse-signals.mjs`).
- The required pi APIs are available: `pi.registerShortcut(Key.ctrl("space"), …)`,
  `ctx.ui.setEditorText()/getEditorText()`, `ctx.ui.setStatus()`,
  `ctx.ui.notify()`, and `pi.sendUserMessage()`.
- Related precedent: the **speak** skill (`SA-0MRHSXIT00089DQ3`) is the inverse
  (text-to-speech) direction and uses a similar external-process bridge.
- faster-whisper is **not** installed in this environment. `arecord` exists but
  the current environment reports *no soundcards*; `ffmpeg`, `sox`, `parecord`
  and `pactl` are absent.
- No existing voice-input/STT work item or code (searched worklog and repo).

## Desired change

Add a new pi extension `pi-client/voice-input/` that:

1. Registers a configurable shortcut (default `Ctrl+Space`) that toggles
   recording.
2. Spawns a capture process (configurable; WSLg/PulseAudio-friendly default)
   producing 16 kHz mono PCM, and frames it for both transcription and
   energy-based silence detection.
3. Runs a persistent `faster-whisper` Python worker on the GPU, feeding
   accumulated audio to produce live partial transcripts.
4. Updates the pi editor live, shows a recording status indicator, and submits
   the final transcript (or leaves an error notification) when the stop trigger
   fires.
5. Ships a dependency/doctor check (faster-whisper import, CUDA availability,
   capture backend, model presence) that emits actionable guidance.
6. Includes docs (`docs/dev/voice-input.md`, extension `README.md`) and unit
   tests (`tests/unit/test-voice-input.mjs`), and is installable by symlink into
   `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `pi-client/voice-input/index.ts` — ExtensionAPI entry: shortcut registration, recording state machine, editor updates, auto-send, status/notifications.
- `pi-client/voice-input/recorder.ts` — spawns the capture command, frames 16 kHz PCM, computes per-frame RMS, drives silence/pause detection.
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper-client.ts` — persistent worker lifecycle and line-delimited JSON protocol (start/feed/finalise/stop).
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py` — loads faster-whisper once (device/compute type from config) and transcribes incoming PCM chunks.
- `pi-client/voice-input/config.ts` — resolves settings/env (keybinding, model, device, compute type, silence threshold/ms, capture command).
- `pi-client/voice-input/doctor.ts` — preflight dependency/CUDA/backend/model checks with actionable messages.
- `pi-client/voice-input/README.md` — install, WSL/CUDA prerequisites, usage, troubleshooting.
- `docs/dev/voice-input.md` — design, protocol, configuration reference.
- `tests/unit/test-voice-input.mjs` — unit tests for the state machine, silence detection, partial replacement, toggle, and protocol.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — (optional) symlink the new extension into `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`.

## Related work

- `SA-0MRHSXIT00089DQ3` — Create a speak skill for text-to-speech (TTS) audio generation and playback (inverse direction; precedent for an external-process audio bridge).
- `SA-0MTWOYFLU004LB2R` — Add TTS to the standup skill (related audio tooling).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MLQ904LV1D1V8ZW** – Unit Tests and Manual E2E Script (completed)
- **SA-0MPKYR7SS000CO2J** – Ralph status command produces inconsistent reports (completed)
- **SA-0MKYE40VG1V2DTOX** – Agent error: 'wl show --thread' missing when running /impplement (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: again, auto, captures, com, create (+11 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: again, auto, com, create, extension (+8 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — matched: auto, com, create, editor, extension (+8 more)

> Note: the automated matches above are keyword-frequency noise (audit tooling,
> unrelated Ralph/status items); the manually curated entries are the
> genuinely related work.

## Risks and assumptions

- **VRAM limit (4 GB)** — `large-v3` may OOM; default `small` and document
  model trade-offs. *Mitigation*: automatic CPU `int8` fallback + clear errors.
- **WSL audio fragility** — capture may fail without WSLg/PulseAudio. *Mitigation*:
  configurable capture command + doctor check + actionable notification.
- **Ctrl+Space interception** — terminal/IME may swallow the key. *Mitigation*:
  configurable keybinding, documented alternative, `/voice-input` command fallback.
- **Partial-transcription latency** — naive re-transcription of a growing buffer
  can be slow. *Mitigation*: bounded sliding window / periodic cadence; tune in
  implementation.
- **Assumption**: "same as if I typed it" means the transcript is submitted as a
  normal user message via `pi.sendUserMessage()`, honouring pi's current
  steering/follow-up mode when busy.
- **Assumption**: live partial text is desired (the operator compared behaviour
  to typing), so partials update the editor while speaking.
- **Scope-creep risk**: multi-language selection, speaker diarisation,
  wake-word activation and cloud STT are explicitly out of scope; capture them
  as separate work items if raised.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Which faster-whisper model/hardware should be the default? — Answer
  (operator): "Yes I have a GPU CUDA to target". Research: `nvidia-smi` in this
  environment reports an NVIDIA RTX 3050 with 4 GB VRAM and CUDA 13.2 driver.
  Default chosen: `small` + `cuda` + `float16`, with CPU `int8` fallback.
  Source: interactive reply + `nvidia-smi`.
- Q: Platform scope — Linux-only or cross-platform? — Answer (operator): "We can
  target Linux with WSL". Research: `arecord` present but no soundcard detected
  here; WSLg/PulseAudio is the expected capture path. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: When auto-send fires while pi is busy, should it steer, queue, or stay in
  the editor? — Answer (operator): "The behavior when sending should be the same
  as if I typed it in". Interpretation: submit as a normal user message and let
  pi's configured steering/follow-up mode apply. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: Should partial text stream live into the editor, or appear only on stop? —
  Answer (operator, implied by "same as if I typed it in"): live partial text.
  This is a documented assumption; revisit if undesired. Source: interactive
  reply (implicit).

## Post-audit recovery note (2026-09-27, audit run 2178s)

The automated `/skill:audit` run on 2026-09-26 failed for **infrastructure
reasons**, not because of any defect in the voice-input work:

- The local proxy was in `cheap` mode (`AUDIT_PARALLELISM=1`) while several
  audits ran concurrently; the Phase 1 parent screen fell back to `partial`
  because the audit concurrency queue saturated (no slot within 90s).
- The Phase 2 deep-analysis output could not be parsed (all 8 ACs marked
  `partial`) and the test-failure child's Phase 2 deep analysis timed out.
- The generated `Ready to close: No` verdict is therefore
  **fallback-tainted (not a genuine model assessment)** and the runner was
  required to restore the pre-audit state rather than demote.
- The runner's terminal lifecycle transition then failed with
  `Invalid status/stage combination: status "blocked" is not compatible with
  stage "in_review"`, leaving the item `blocked`/`in_review`. It has been
  recovered manually to `blocked`/`plan_complete`.

Side effects of the failed run (documented for the producer):

- The full project suite was **red** at the audited HEAD (4 commands, 11
  failures, all in the audit/test infrastructure); triage created 11 critical
  `test-failure` items and linked
  `SA-0MUIXZKH500624QM` as a blocking child/dependency of this item.
- The failed parent audit persisted short `Ready to close: No` child audits
  to the five voice-input children (because they carry no parseable AC
  heading), which reverted them from `completed`/`in_review` to
  `open`/`plan_complete` (two now `blocked`). Their implementation is
  complete and merged to `dev`.

This note intentionally changes the description hash so the stored
fallback-tainted audit becomes stale: **re-run the audit with `--force`**
(and preferably when the proxy is not saturated and the suite is green).

## Failure Signature

- Test name: tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli
- Failing commit: 0d0d0fc0ab144e796ce616d8f5436e6a70dd4bed
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
live-repo mutation detected during tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli:
  added config   branch.wl-SA-0MU32TAMB007HI99-r1-audit-debug-log-mislabels-every-succe.merge=refs/heads/dev
  added config   branch.wl-SA-0MU32TAMB007HI99-r1-audit-debug-log-mislabels-every-succe.remote=.
```

## Root Cause (evidence-backed)

The named test is **not defective** — it is the *victim* of a false positive in
the live-repo mutation guard (F5, SA-0MUG30JSE0069JEQ). The guard fails whichever
test finishes next when the main checkout's shared `.git/config` changes mid-run:

- `implement.py::git_worktree_add()` runs `git worktree add --track -b <branch> <path> dev`,
  which writes `branch.<branch>.remote=.` and `branch.<branch>.merge=refs/heads/dev`
  into the **main checkout's shared `.git/config`**.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::snapshot_repo_state()` captures **all** local config
  (`git config --local --list`).
- `fingerprint()` (`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py:414`) and `diff_snapshots()`
  (`:446-455`) filter agent-worktree **refs** via `excluded_refs`, but do **not**
  filter the matching `branch.<excluded-ref>.{remote,merge}` config keys.
- `live_repo_guard.py::pytest_runtest_teardown` therefore sees a config diff caused
  by a concurrent agent's `implement.py start` and fails the next test to finish —
  here the ~6.7 s cleanup integration test.

This is the same guard false-positive class as SA-0MUILGH5E007X627 (worktree-root
anchoring / ref churn) and SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH (shared `refs/stash` churn), and
reproduces the root cause first identified for SA-0MUIP4PAG005YI91 (closed as a
false positive without a guard fix).

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout 0d0d0fc0ab144e796ce616d8f5436e6a70dd4bed`
2. Run the failing test: `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings -k tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli` (or equivalent command)
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item. Because the guard misattributes a concurrent
worktree's config churn to an unrelated test, the failure is non-deterministic and
will recur on any shared host with more than one active agent session.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli` passes when run against the latest `dev`.
2. The live-repo mutation guard no longer reports a mutation for `branch.<worktree-branch>.remote` / `.merge` config churn written by a concurrent `implement.py start` / worktree registration. Verification: a test mutates the shared `.git/config` branch keys for a branch present in `excluded_refs` and asserts `diff_snapshots(before, after)["changed"] is False` and `fingerprint()` is unchanged.
3. Genuine in-place checkout mutations are still reported (moved `HEAD`/branch ref, tracked-file edit, untracked non-ignored file, unrelated config change); the existing guard contract tests remain green.
4. Documentation describing the guard's exclusion surface (e.g. `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` and the `git_sandbox.py` docstring) is updated to state that worktree-branch config keys are excluded.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MUILGH5E007X627** — live-repo guard false-positives inside an agent worktree (concurrent worktree ref churn) (open)
- **SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH** — Live-repo guard: shared refs/stash causes spurious mutation failures across concurrent worktrees (open)
- **SA-0MUIP4PAG005YI91** — same failure signature; closed as a false positive without a guard fix (completed)

## Key Files:

- `tests/test_cleanup_integration.py`
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`
- `scripts/cleanup/prune_local_branches.py`
- `scripts/cleanup/cleanup_stale_remote_branches.py`
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.

## Summary

The shared main checkout's git identity was left as the 2026-09-26 leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident's commit identity (`user.name=T`, `user.email=t@t.com`). `wl sync` refused to merge incoming Worklog data because the author-identity gate rejects commits whose author email does not match the configured `user.email`:

```
✗ Sync failed: Refusing to merge worklog data from
refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data: 1 incoming commit(s) fail the
author-identity gate.
- ed506bef: author email '250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com' does
  not match configured user.email 't@t.com'
```

Symptom observed during SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX (2026-09-26T23:2x). The identity has since been corrected to the global `Sorra the Orc <250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com>` and `wl sync` now completes, but this item exists to verify the restoration is durable and cannot silently regress (the bad identity came from the incident's `.git/config` rewrite, which is exactly the class SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX guards against).

**Source:** discovered-from:SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX

## Goal

Ensure `wl sync` completes on the main checkout with a correct, durable git identity, so Worklog data is not silently stranded by the author-identity gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `git config user.name` / `user.email` on the main checkout resolve to the canonical agent identity (not `T` / `t@t.com`), at local or global scope, and `git config --local --get user.email` returns empty (no incident-era local override).
- [ ] `git config --local --get core.bare` is `false` on the shared checkout.
- [ ] `wl sync` exits 0 and reports success, with a re-run being a no-op (idempotent).
- [ ] A guard/setup check detects and reports a mismatched `user.email` before `wl sync` runs (or in the installer), so the failure is actionable rather than a silent sync refusal; the guard is exercised by an automated test that proves it fires on a mismatched identity.
- [ ] The verification steps are recorded in a comment with the exact commands and observed output.

## Notes

- The incident-era identity is a residual effect of the corrupted `.git/config` documented in `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` (recovery playbook §9.4 step 4 verifies identity).
- Do not weaken the author-identity gate; restore the identity instead.

data.description: Full test suites are being launched in overlapping concurrency without any coordination. Current pattern: 3+ concurrent vitest runs each spawning ~16 fork workers at ~400 MB, plus 5+ overlapping pytest/audit runs. This contributes to 566 processes and 1986 threads with load averaging 44 on a 16-core box (3× oversubscription). Solution: implement a global test-job semaphore/queue so only N test suites run simultaneously (suggest N=2), with a config file and a wrapper script (e.g. pace-run.sh) that acquires a lock before launching tests and releases it on completion. Integrate with existing test skills so they use the pacers instead of spawning raw.

# Ship skill: let a release-ready parent override (or absorb) `needsProducerReview` on its children

## Problem

The ship release close step (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`) **skips every item with `needsProducerReview === true`**:

```js
const toClose = items.filter((item) => item.needsProducerReview === false);
```

For a **child** item that was flagged `needsProducerReview=true`, this leaves the child in `in_review` and — because `wl close --force` is then refused to avoid sweeping it — can leave the **parent** unreleased-in-tracking even after the code has shipped.

### Motivating case (ContextHub v1.0.16)

- Parent `WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28` (`in_review`, audit passed, code on `main`) has 5 children.
- 4 children were closed; the 5th, `WL-0MU8807BI008C9ME`, is `in_review` with `needsProducerReview=true`.
- Result: the parent cannot be closed and remains `in_review` despite shipping. Every other blocker was resolved.

The current scoping rules (SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H) already say a child's audit/review is **covered by an audit-ready `in_review` parent** — so a covered child's `needsProducerReview` flag should not outlive / contradict that parent's ready-to-release determination.

## Desired behaviour

When the release skill evaluates a **child** with `needsProducerReview=true`, it must resolve the flag against the parent's readiness:

1. **Parent overrides (default when the parent is release-ready):** if the child's nearest `in_review` ancestor is an audit-ready release candidate (`readyToClose === true`), the skill may **clear the child's `needsProducerReview` flag** (set `false`) and record a comment on the child explaining the override, then close it. The parent's passing audit is what authorises the override.
2. **Genuine attention required:** if the child genuinely needs producer attention (unresolved question, ambiguous requirement, manual approval owed), the skill must **escalate to the parent** instead: set `needsProducerReview=true` on the parent and add a comment **enumerating the child id(s)** that require attention. The parent then blocks the release through the existing producer-review gate (Step 3.6) — which is the correct fail-safe.
3. The override must **never** be authorised by status alone: it requires the parent's passing audit (`readyToClose === true`). A non-`in_review` parent or an unaudited parent must not silently clear a child flag.
4. Every flag change (child cleared, or parent escalated) must be **logged** with a comment naming the authorising parent/audit or the children that need attention.
5. `--dry-run` must report the planned overrides/escalations without mutating any work item.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A child with `needsProducerReview=true` under an audit-ready `in_review` parent is closed after its flag is cleared, with an explanatory comment on the child.
2. A child that genuinely needs attention causes the parent to be flagged `needsProducerReview=true` with a comment naming the child(ren); the parent then fails the producer-review gate.
3. Clearing a child flag is refused when the parent is not `in_review` or its audit is not `readyToClose`.
4. `--dry-run` performs no mutations and reports the intended child overrides and parent escalations.
5. Unit tests inject `getCandidateItemsFn`/`getDescendantsFn`/`runCloseCommand` boundaries and never mutate the live worklog.
6. `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and `SKILL.md` document the override/escalation contract.
7. `npm run build` and existing suites pass.

## Notes

- Related: SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H (parent-coverage / out-of-scope child rules), SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP (close step falsely refuses when descendants are already `stage: done`).
- The two changes are complementary: SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP stops refusing on already-done descendants; this item resolves the remaining `needsProducerReview` child case.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSKB6WA8009XKTX** – Audit: refresh measured baseline and performance docs (completed)
- **SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E** – [CRITICAL] Audit runner has circular dependency — child audit verdict blocks parent regardless of stage (completed)
- **SA-0MLQ8YP2X0I2XJ0M** – Prerequisite Validation and Error Handling (completed)

- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alone, already, ancestor (+124 more)

## Intake blocked: producer review required — scope ambiguous after prior implementation

I ran the intake evaluation for **Implement test job pacing to prevent resource oversubscription (SA-0MUJL211C008GHMZ)**. The core mechanism in the seed is **already implemented** by other work items, while the specific residual gaps are tracked in three separate open items. The intended scope of *this* item is therefore ambiguous; choosing for you risks either duplicating completed work or silently expanding scope. Questions are at the end.

### What already exists (evidence)

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — flock-based cross-process counting semaphore (SA-0MSAK2P3J0065POO).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — acquires a host-wide `"test"` semaphore around each real suite execution: `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (default **2**), `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (default 600 s); cache hits never consume a slot. Concurrent runs are capped and wait bounded (SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG, completed; commit `dc7ffd79`). Integration tests in `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py`.
- Audit-side concurrency is separately bounded by an `"audit"` semaphore (independently namespaced).
- `.pi/test-config.json` exists but only sets `timeoutPerCommand` — there is **no** pacing config file and **no** `pace-run.sh` wrapper in the tree.

### What is NOT yet paced (the residual gap)

`run_tests.py` is the only caller that acquires the test semaphore. Two execution paths call `test_cache.run_cached(...)` directly and therefore bypass it:

1. `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_run_changed_scope_pytest` (~L2026) and `run_tests`, used by the `implement.py finish` gate. `implement.py` contains **no** `Semaphore` usage.
2. `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_run_tests_via_test_skill` (~L2713, `force=True`), already tracked by SA-0MUJK94QN0015925.

### Overlapping open items

- **SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2** — browser/vitest contention: `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2` lets two full suites starve each other (exit 137/124); proposes serialising browser suites to 1 / a context-aware ceiling.
- **SA-0MUJK94QN0015925** — audit F3 auto-execution bypasses the test semaphore (`run_cached(force=True)`).
- **SA-0MUG47DYG006TV40** — cold-cache child-audit cascade recursively executes the full suite.
- **SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF** (in progress) — multi-agent audit/test coordination / blocking.

### Questions

**Q1 — Residual scope.** Given SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG already delivered the shared semaphore + `run_tests.py` integration, what is the intended scope of SA-0MUJL211C008GHMZ?

- **A (Recommended):** Treat it as the umbrella/epic that ties the remaining gaps together — decompose into children for the audit F3 bypass, the implement gate bypass, and the browser-suite contention — and reconcile the overlapping open items.
- **B:** Narrow it to the genuinely unbuilt parts named in the seed: a shared pacing config file + a `pace-run.sh` wrapper, and route the remaining raw spawners (implement.py, audit F3) through the pacer.
- **C:** It is a duplicate / superseded by SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG — close it and let the three specific open items stand alone.
- **D:** Other (please specify).

**Q2 — Ownership of the bypasses.** Should this item own routing *all* test executions through the pacer (including the implement gate, which has no item yet), or only define/enforce the pacer and leave each call site to its own item?

- **A (Recommended if Q1 = A):** This item owns all pacer call-site integration.
- **B:** Define/enforce the pacer only; per-skill call sites stay with their own items (audit → SA-0MUJK94QN0015925; implement → new item).

**Q3 — Ceiling semantics and config.** The seed proposes a config file with N=2. `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` / `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` env vars already exist. Which is intended?

- **A (Recommended):** Keep the env-var mechanism, add an optional committed config file that feeds it, and make browser/Chromium suites serialise to 1 (absorbs SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2).
- **B:** No new config file — env vars only; keep a static host-wide N=2.
- **C:** Other.

Once these are answered I will complete the intake (draft brief, AC coverage, effort/risk). Flagging for producer review now.
